The median age of Singaporeans increased from 34.1 years in 2000 to an estimated 42.4 by 2020.
The population growth rate in 2025 is projected at 0.63 percent.
The Population of Singapore attained a value of 6,036,860 people in 2024. Singapore’s total population has exceeded six million.
Work permit holders contribute 44 per cent of non-resident population. One-third of the non-resident population comprises mainly migrant domestic workers, dependants and students.
Migration increases population by 29,844 people yearly. The average annual number of citizen marriages in the last five years is 22,700.
The all-time high population for Singapore is projected to be 8,609,518 in 2050. The record low population for Singapore was 1,022,100 in 1950.

Annualised population growth rate of 1.1 per cent over the last five years was slightly higher than the 0.8 per cent over the preceding five-year period. Annualised population growth rate was 1.1 per cent over the past five years.
Citizen population increased by 0.7% from 3.61 million to 3.64 million between June 2023 and June 2024. Citizen population rose from 3.61 million in June 2023 to 3.64 million in June 2024.
The Singapore population was 5.9 million people in Jun 2023. 5.92 million total population of Singapore as of June 2023. Singapore’s total population stood at 6.04 million as at June 2024.
Permanent resident population grew by 1.2 per cent from June 2023 to June 2024.
1.6% growth in Singapore Citizens from June 2022 to June 2023.

315,400 population increase in the 1970–1980 period was due to natural increase. Net migration increased to nearly 200,000 in the 1980–1990 period. Net migrant number of over 600,000 in the 1990–2000 period.
Net migration accounted for nearly two-thirds of the population increase in the 1990–2000 period.
The average annual growth rate was 4.4% from 1947 to 1957.
Non-residents were 25.7% of the population in 2010.
There were 1,925 Bugis in Singapore in January 1824.

The total population of Singapore from 2019 to 2050 is projected to grow from 5 million in 2019 to 8.61 million in 2050. In June 2023, the population was 5.9 million, and it is estimated to be 6.04 million in 2024.
In June 2023, Singapore had 3.61 million citizens, a 1.6% increase from June 2022, and 0.54 million permanent residents, a 3.7% increase.
Singapore records 49,414 births annually, with new birth cohorts ranging from 35,000 to 40,000.
Singapore's fertility rate was 1.4 in 1986, 1.65 for Chinese in 1990, and in 2022, the TFR was 1.04, with Chinese at 0.87 and Indian at 1.01.
The population of Singapore is projected at 5.83 million in 2024. The data reached an all-time high of 6.0 million people in Jun 2024.
1.77 million non-residents as of June 2023. Singapore’s total population rose by 2 per cent from June 2023 to June 2024, reaching 6.04 million.

Annualised population growth rate was 1.1 per cent over the past five years. Population growth was stable, ranging from 1.3% to 1.9% per annum during the second phase (1970s to mid-1980s).
Singapore experienced its highest birth rate in 1957 at 42.7 per thousand individuals.
The number of non-residents grew from 30,900 in 1970 to 797,900 in 2005. Non-residents were 18.3% of the population in 2005.

Foreign workers in non-CMP sectors saw an 8.8% increase year on year. Approvals for PRs aged 31+ increased by 15.6%. The approval rate for citizens aged 40+ increased by 26.2% in 2022 compared to the previous year.
Singapore's total population including foreigners with permits was 5.0 million in 2009. 3.64 million are citizens in Singapore. 1.86 million are non-residents in Singapore.
Fertility reached replacement level in 1975. Fertility is below 1.3. The lowest recorded TFR for the Indian population was 1.01 in 2022. Singapore total fertility rate (TFR) was 1.20 in 2012.
